finite accepts a NaN
equivalent: belt-and-braces with the guard inside `charge`. `finite` exists to turn a bare `f64` price into the same `Option` shape the other prices already have, and `charge` then accepts a price only under `Some(e) if e.is_finite()` — so a `finite` that passed a NaN through would hand `charge` a `Some(NaN)` that it rejects for the same reason, naming the term unpriced and refusing the total exactly as before.
